references.text: The charges against Jesus began already when he was brought before Pilate. In Luke 23:2, the chief priests and scribes formulate the specific accusations that they now repeat forcefully to Herod.
The chief priests and scribes had already interrogated Jesus in the Council (Luke 22:66-71), and it is the same accusers who now stand and accuse him before Herod.
In Mark 15:3, it is described that the chief priests brought many charges against Jesus before Pilate, which corresponds to the earnest accusation described in Luke 23:10.
In Matthew 27:12, it is told that Jesus did not answer anything when the chief priests and elders accused him, which is a parallel to the persistent accusation from the religious leaders.
The pattern of eager accusations from Jewish religious leaders against an innocent person repeats itself in Acts 24:5-8, where Paul is accused in a similar way before the authorities.

The psalmist describes in Psalm 22:13 enemies surrounding the suffering one – a prophetic depiction that finds its fulfillment in the violent accusations of the chief priests and scribes against Jesus.
The prophecy in Isaiah 53:7 about the Lord's suffering servant who was afflicted but did not open his mouth forms the background for the scene where Jesus is accused fiercely but remains silent.
Already in Luke 11:53-54, the scribes and Pharisees began to press in on Jesus and try to catch him in something he said – that hostility culminates here in the earnest accusations before Herod.
